passages.title: Section I: Use of English
passages.content:
Millions of Americans and foreigners see G.I. Joe as a mindless war toy, the symbol of American military adventurism, but that's not how it used to be. To the men and women who [1] in World War II and the people they liberated, the G.I. was the [2] man grown into hero, the poor farm kid torn away from his home, the guy who [3] all the burdens of battle, who slept in cold foxholes, who went without the [4] of food and shelter, who stuck it out and drove back the Nazi reign of murder. This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid, [5] an average guy, up [6] the best trained, best equipped, fiercest, most brutal enemies seen in centuries.

His name isn't much. G.I. is just a military abbreviation [7] Government Issue, and it was on all of the articles [8] to soldiers. And Joe? A common name for a guy who never [9] it to the top. Joe Blow, Joe Palooka, Joe Magrac... a working class name. The United States has [10] had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe.

G.I. Joe had a [11] career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops. He appears as a character, or a [12] of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe, based on the last days of war correspondent Ernie Pyle. Some of the soldiers Pyle [13] portrayed themselves in the film. Pyle was famous for covering the [14] side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers, not how many miles were [15] or what towns were captured or liberated. His reports [16] the "Willie" cartoons of famed Stars and Stripes artist Bill Maulden. Both men [17] the dirt and exhaustion of war, the [18] of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep. [19] Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, [20] the most important person in their lives.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 1
passages.content:
Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned. School districts across the country, most recently Los Angeles Unified, are revising their thinking on this educational ritual. Unfortunately, L.A. Unified has produced an inflexible policy which mandates that with the exception of some advanced courses, homework may no longer count for more than 10% of a student's academic grade.

This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework. But the policy is unclear and contradictory. Certainly, no homework should be assigned that students cannot complete on their own or that they cannot do without expensive equipment. But if the district is essentially giving a pass to students who do not do their homework because of complicated family lives, it is going riskily close to the implication that standards need to be lowered for poor children.

District administrators say that homework will still be a part of schooling; teachers are allowed to assign as much of it as they want. But with homework counting for no more than 10% of their grades, students can easily skip half their homework and see very little difference on their report cards. Some students might do well on state tests without completing their homework, but what about the students who performed well on the tests and did their homework? It is quite possible that the homework helped. Yet rather than empowering teachers to find what works best for their students, the policy imposes a flat, across-the-board rule.

At the same time, the policy addresses none of the truly thorny questions about homework. If the district finds homework to be unimportant to its students' academic achievement, it should move to reduce or eliminate the assignments, not make them count for almost nothing. Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion of the grade. Meanwhile, this policy does nothing to ensure that the homework students receive is meaningful or appropriate to their age and the subject, or that teachers are not assigning more than they are willing to review and correct.

The homework rules should be put on hold while the school board, which is responsible for setting educational policy, looks into the matter and conducts public hearings. It is not too late for L.A. Unified to do homework right.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 2
passages.content:
Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is pervasive in our young girls' lives. It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls' identity to appearance. Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not only innocent but as evidence of innocence. Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of imagination about girls' lives and interests.

Girls' attraction to pink may seem unavoidable, somehow encoded in their DNA, but according to Jo Paoletti, an associate professor of American Studies, it is not. Children were not colour-coded at all until the early 20th century: in the era before domestic washing machines all babies wore white as a practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them. What's more, both boys and girls wore what were thought of as gender-neutral dresses. When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated with strength. Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity. It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant children's marketing strategy, that pink fully came into its own, when it began to seem inherently attractive to girls, part of what defined them as female, at least for the first few critical years.

I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.

Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a "third stepping stone" between infant wear and older kids' clothes. It was only after "toddler" became a common shoppers' term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage. Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits. And one of the easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences—or invent them where they did not previously exist.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 3
passages.content:
In 2010, a federal judge shook America's biotech industry to its core. Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades—by 2005 some 20% of human genes were patented. But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable. Executives were violently agitated. The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a "preliminary step" in a longer battle.

On July 29th they were relieved, at least temporarily. A federal appeals court overturned the prior decision, ruling that Myriad Genetics could indeed hold patents to two genes that help forecast a woman's risk of breast cancer. The chief executive of Myriad, a company in Utah, said the ruling was a blessing to firms and patients alike.

But as companies continue their attempts at personalised medicine, the courts will remain rather busy. The Myriad case itself is probably not over. Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's. A growing number seem to agree. Last year a federal task-force urged reform for patents related to genetic tests. In October the Department of Justice filed a brief in the Myriad case, arguing that an isolated DNA molecule "is no less a product of nature... than are cotton fibres that have been separated from cotton seeds."

Despite the appeals court's decision, big questions remain unanswered. For example, it is unclear whether the sequencing of a whole genome violates the patents of individual genes within it. The case may yet reach the Supreme Court.

As the industry advances, however, other suits may have an even greater impact. Companies are unlikely to file many more patents for human DNA molecules—most are already patented or in the public domain. Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy. Companies are eager to win patents for "connecting the dots," explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO.

Their success may be determined by a suit related to this issue, brought by the Mayo Clinic, which the Supreme Court will hear in its next term. The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents. Each meeting was packed.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part A - Text 4
passages.content:
The great recession may be over, but this era of high joblessness is probably beginning. Before it ends, it will likely change the life course and character of a generation of young adults. And ultimately, it is likely to reshape our politics, our culture, and the character of our society for years.

No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster. Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others. In limited respects, perhaps the recession will leave society better off. At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending.

But for the most part, these benefits seem thin, uncertain, and far off. In The Moral Consequences of Economic Growth, the economic historian Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms. Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes.

Income inequality usually falls during a recession, but it has not shrunk in this one. Indeed, this period of economic weakness may reinforce class divides, and decrease opportunities to cross them—especially for young people. The research of Till Von Wachter, the economist at Columbia University, suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind.

In the Internet age, it is particularly easy to see the resentment that has always been hidden within American society. More difficult, in the moment, is discerning precisely how these lean times are affecting society's character. In many respects, the U.S. was more socially tolerant entering this recession than at any time in its history, and a variety of national polls on social conflict since then have shown mixed results. We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric. But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend.

passages.title: Section II: Reading Comprehension Part B
passages.content:
"Universal history, the history of what man has accomplished in this world, is at bottom the History of the Great Men who have worked here," wrote the Victorian sage Thomas Carlyle. Well, not any more it is not.

Suddenly, Britain looks to have fallen out with its favorite historical form. This could be no more than a passing literary craze, but it also points to a broader truth about how we now approach the past: less concerned with learning from our forefathers and more interested in feeling their pain. Today, we want empathy, not inspiration.

From the earliest days of the Renaissance, the writing of history meant recounting the exemplary lives of great men. In 1337, Petrarch began work on his rambling writing De Viris Illustribus—On Famous Men, highlighting the virtus (or virtue) of classical heroes. Petrarch celebrated their greatness in conquering fortune and rising to the top. This was the biographical tradition which Niccolò Machiavelli turned on its head. In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue, mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders.

Over time, the attributes of greatness shifted. The Romantics commemorated the leading painters and authors of their day, stressing the uniqueness of the artist's personal experience rather than public glory. By contrast, the Victorian author Samuel Smiles wrote Self-Help as a catalogue of the worthy lives of engineers, industrialists and explorers. "The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble and manly character, exhibit," wrote Smiles, "what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself." His biographies of James Watt, Richard Arkwright and Josiah Wedgwood were held up as beacons to guide the working man through his difficult life.

This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte. These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals.

Not everyone was convinced by such bombast. "The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles," wrote Marx and Engels in The Communist Manifesto. For them, history did nothing, it possessed no immense wealth nor waged battles: "It is man, real, living man who does all that." And history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle. As such, it needed to appreciate the economic realities, the social contexts and power relations in which each epoch stood. For: "Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly found, given and transmitted from the past."

This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past. In place of Thomas Carlyle, Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm. History from below stood alongside biographies of great men. Whole new realms of understanding—from gender to race to cultural studies—were opened up as scholars unpicked the multiplicity of lost societies. And it transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [1] in the passage:
questions.explanation: 【命题解密】句内语义与熟词僻义。定位至第②句“To the men and women who 1 in World War II and the people they liberated...”。结合后文“解放”可知，此处指的是在二战中服役并解放沦陷区的人们。serve作不及物动词时常与in连用，表示“服役，参军”，与in World War II构成完美搭配，故选[A]。[B] performed意为“执行；表现”，若表示执行任务需接宾语tasks等；[C] rebelled意为“反叛；反抗”，与被其解放的人民语境矛盾；[D] betrayed意为“出卖；背叛”，亦与语境不符。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [2] in the passage:
questions.explanation: 【命题解密】上下文语义与形容词辨析。空格处作定语修饰man，后文用“the poor farm kid torn away from his home”做同位语补充说明。the common man是英语中的经典固定表达，意为“普通人；平民百姓”，与后文“grown into hero（成长为平民英雄）”形成鲜明对比，展现了平凡人造就非凡伟业的立意，故选[B]。[A] actual强调“实际的；真实的”，无法形成对比；[C] special（特殊的）与平民小子语境相反；[D] normal（正常的；精神正常的）不能体现平民阶层含义。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [3] in the passage:
questions.explanation: 【命题解密】句内语义与动词辨析。定语从句结构为“who [3] all the burdens of battle”。bear the burdens of battle为英语经典搭配，意为“承受/挑起战斗的重担”，bear的过去式为bore，故选[D]。[A] loaded通常构成load sb with sth结构；[B] eased意为“减轻，缓和”，与前线作战的艰苦现实相反；[C] removed意为“免除，消除”，士兵不可能免除战斗重担。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [4] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］名词词义辨析与战地生活语境。
［解题思路］空格前后指出士兵们在极端艰苦的条件下持续作战，“甚至常常缺少食物与庇护所等最基本的[4]（生活必需品）”。the necessities of food and shelter 为习惯表达，指维持基本生存所必需的物资，故选［A］necessities。
［错项排除］［B］facilities（设施、设备，多指硬件场馆或公共装置）、［C］commodities（大宗日用商品，偏商业贸易属性）及［D］properties（财产、房地产）均无法精准传达战时匮乏基本生存保障之意。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [5] in the passage:
questions.explanation: 【命题解密】句内逻辑关系。空格前为“This was not a volunteer soldier, not someone well paid”，空格后为“an average guy”。前后构成典型的“not... not... but...”否定与肯定对比结构，意为“不是……也不是……而是……”，故选[C] but。[A] and表顺承；[B] nor常用于neither...nor...或否定句后表示“也不”；[D] hence表因果关系。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [6] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［定位/考点］高频固定动词短语搭配与句内语义。
［解题思路］空格所在定语成分修饰前线战士（an average guy），刻画其“正面[6]数百年来所见最训练有素、装备最精良也最凶残的敌人”。be up against 为固定习语搭配，意为“直面、面临（严峻困难或强敌劲旅）”，契合双方军力对比悬殊的战地语境，故选［D］against。
［错项排除］［A］for、［B］into 与［C］from 均无法置于 be up... 之后构成“直面强敌竞争或挑战”的固定语义搭配。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [7] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与现在分词辨析。
［精准定位］G.I. is just a military abbreviation [7] Government Issue...
［解题思路］句中指出 G.I. 只是一个军用缩略语，[7] Government Issue。对比可见，G 与 I 恰好是 Government Issue 两词的首字母组合，因此 Government Issue 正是在解释缩略语 G.I. 的完整含义。meaning 意为“意思是；表示……的意思”，现在分词短语 meaning Government Issue 作后置定语修饰 abbreviation，完美契合“缩写—全称解释”的语义关系，故选[B]。
［错项排除］[A] implying（暗示；暗指）侧重间接或隐含地表达含义，而 G.I. 与 Government Issue 存在直接明了的首字母对应关系，并非“暗指”，故排除；[C] symbolizing（象征；代表）侧重以具体事物表达抽象意义，而此处并非“具体—抽象”的象征关系，而是“缩写—全称”关系，故排除；[D] claiming 可表“声称（未经证实的观点）”或“认领；索取”，句中修饰“缩略语”而非“士兵”，逻辑均不符，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [8] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］动词短语搭配与句内语义。
［精准定位］...and it was on all of the articles [8] to soldiers.
［解题思路］空格所在分句指出，G.I. 这个缩略语印在 [8] 给士兵的所有物品（articles）上。结合前文 G.I. 的全称 Government Issue（政府配发/发放）可知，这些物品是由政府或军方发放给士兵的。handed out（分发、发放）作过去分词短语 handed out to soldiers 修饰 articles，准确呼应 Government Issue 的内涵，故选[A]。
［错项排除］[B] turned over（移交；转交所有权/管理权）侧重把控制权或管理权正式交给他人，并非政府向普通士兵分发军需物品，故排除；[C] brought back（带回；使恢复）无法与“物品发往士兵”的语境搭配，故排除；[D] passed down（世代相传；自上而下流传）多指传统、财产或经验的代际传承，不合句意，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [9] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］固定习语搭配与上下文语义。
［精准定位］A common name for a guy who never [9] it to the top.
［解题思路］句中解释“Joe”是一个代表普通人的常见名字，他从未 [9] 过社会顶层；后文紧接着列举 Joe Blow、Joe Palooka、Joe Magrac 等工人阶级常用名予以印证。make it 为固定习语，意为“获得成功；闯出名堂”，never made it to the top 意为“从未成功攀上事业或社会巅峰”，契合平民与工人阶级语境，故选[C]。
［错项排除］[A] pushed 与虚指宾语 it 搭配时多表示“勉强；得寸进尺（push it）”，push sth to the top 需接具体实物，不合句意，故排除；[B] got（get it）意为“明白；得到”，其中的 it 需实指前文事物，且不与 to the top 搭配表达成功登顶，故排除；[D] managed 表“设法完成”时需接不定式（manage to do）或实指宾语，不能与虚指 it 构成 manage it to the top，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [10] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与否定副词用法。
［精准定位］The United States has [10] had a president or vice-president or secretary of state Joe.
［解题思路］本句作为佐证指出：美国 [10] 有过名叫“Joe”的总统、副总统或国务卿（均属最高层政要）。与前两句“never made it to the top（从未登上顶层）”“a working class name（工人阶级名字）”一脉相承，此处句中无其他否定词，应填入自身表完全否定含义的副词 never（从未），故选[B]。
［错项排除］[A] ever 意为“曾经；在任何时候”，本身不含否定意味，在无其他否定词的肯定陈述句中不能表“从未”，故排除；[C] either 作副词表“（用于否定句末）也”，前文并无否定词且位置不符，故排除；[D] neither 表“也不”，多用于承接前句的否定倒装结构（neither did...），不能置于助动词 has 与过去分词 had 之间否定单句，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [11] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与形容词辨析。
［精准定位］G.I. Joe had a [11] career fighting German, Japanese, and Korean troops.
［解题思路］第三段转入对“大兵乔”历史形象的正面颂扬，指出他曾与德军、日军及朝军作战，拥有一段 [11] 的军旅生涯，后被拍成经典电影并深受多国民众敬仰。distinguished 意为“卓越的；杰出的；战功显赫的”，与 career 搭配传神体现作者对其战功与贡献的高度褒奖，故选[D]。
［错项排除］[A] disguised 意为“伪装的；隐蔽的”，与大兵乔公开英勇作战的事迹不符，故排除；[B] disturbed 意为“心神不安的；受到干扰的”，含贬义，与全文赞扬基调相悖，故排除；[C] disputed 意为“有争议的”，原文并未质疑其军旅生涯的功绩，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [12] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］固定搭配与抽象名词辨析。
［精准定位］He appears as a character, or a [12] of American personalities, in the 1945 movie The Story of G.I. Joe...
［解题思路］句意指出，在 1945 年电影《美国大兵乔的故事》中，G.I. Joe 作为一个角色出现，或者说是美国人性格特点的 [12]。结合上文“大兵乔泛指普通美军士兵，乔代表普通美国人”可知，该艺术形象汇聚了诸多普通美国人的性格特质。a collection of 意为“一批；集合”，a collection of American personalities 意为“美国人性格特点的集合”，契合语境，故选[C]。
［错项排除］[A] company 表“陪伴”或“为某一目的聚在一起的一群人”，不能与抽象的“性格特点”搭配，故排除；[B] community 指“社区居民群”或“生物群落”，亦不与抽象性格特征搭配，故排除；[D] colony 指“（同地区）动植物群”或“殖民地”，侧重有生命的生物群体，与无生命的 personalities 无法搭配，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [13] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文语义与动词辨析。
［精准定位］Some of the soldiers Pyle [13] portrayed themselves in the film.
［解题思路］前句交代电影改编自著名战地记者厄尼·派尔（war correspondent Ernie Pyle）生命最后时光的经历；本句指出派尔 [13] 过的一些士兵在影片中本色出演了自己。基于战地记者（记者与一线官兵）的身份定位，“采访”是其核心报道方式，interviewed（采访）最能构建“采访—记录—改编电影”的连贯逻辑，故选[C]。
［错项排除］[A] employed 意为“雇用”，战地记者并非士兵的雇主，逻辑不符，故排除；[B] appointed 意为“任命；委派”，记者无权任命军队士兵，故排除；[D] questioned 虽可译作“提问”，但语体侧重审讯、盘问或官方质询，不适用于记者与战地士兵之间的日常访谈场景，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [14] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内对比语义与熟词僻义。
［精准定位］Pyle was famous for covering the [14] side of the war, writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers...
［解题思路］句中对比表明，派尔因报道战争 [14] 的一面而闻名：他笔下写的是满身泥尘风雪的普通士兵，而非推进了多少英里或攻占了哪些城镇等宏大战事。human 除“人的”外，在此语境下意为“有人情味的；关注普通人处境的”，the human side of the war 与具体的基层士兵形成完美照应，故选[A]。
［错项排除］[B] military（军事的）恰恰对应后文否定成分中“行军英里数、攻占/解放城镇”等纯军事进展，与 not 所引导的对比逻辑相悖，故排除；[C] political（政治的）与 [D] ethical（伦理道德的）均属宏观或抽象层面议题，并非派尔聚焦微观一线士兵冷暖的写作重心，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [15] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］熟词僻义与动宾语义搭配。
［精准定位］...not how many miles were [15] or what towns were captured or liberated.
［解题思路］空格位于与 towns were captured or liberated 并列的分句中，主语为 how many miles（多少英里），共同说明宏观层面的军事战果进展。gain 除基本义“获得；增加”外，可作熟词僻义表“（军队等）向前推进（一段距离）”，可直接接长度单位（如 gain miles），变为被动语态 miles were gained 表示“战线推进了多少英里”，契合语境，故选[D]。
［错项排除］[A] ruined（毁坏；破坏）不能以距离单位“英里”作为承受动作的逻辑宾语，语义不通，故排除；[B] commuted（通勤往返）常与 between/to/from 等地点介词连用描述日常生活上班，不接长度度量且不符战争语境，故排除；[C] patrolled（巡逻；巡查）需以“区域、道路、边境”而非纯距离“多少英里”作宾语（若表距离须为 miles of road were patrolled），且“巡逻”不体现前线推进战果，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [16] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
【考点提炼】上下文语义+动词辨析。
【解题思路】前文指出战地记者 Ernie Pyle 擅长报道战争中普通士兵的真实面貌（writing about the dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers），紧接着空格句说明“他的报道 [16] 著名漫画家 Bill Maulden 的《威利》系列漫画（His reports [16] the 'Willie' cartoons...）”，而后一句进一步解释“两人都聚焦于战争的泥泞与疲惫（Both men... the dirt and exhaustion of war）”。可见 Pyle 的文字报道与 Maulden 的漫画在主题和情感基调上高度一致、相互呼应，[A] paralleled（与……相似/相呼应）最符合语境。
【错项排除】[B] counteracted（抵消，对抗）和 [D] contradicted（反驳，与……相矛盾）均表达对立或相反关系，与下文 Both men 体现的“二者一致”完全相悖；[C] duplicated（复制，完全重复）程度过重，文字报道与漫画属于不同体裁，二者是主题契合与呼应，而非机械复制。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [17] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］上下文呼应与动词辨析。
［精准定位］Both men [17] the dirt and exhaustion of war, the [18] of civilization that the soldiers shared...
［解题思路］前两句先介绍战地记者派尔擅长刻画满身泥雪的士兵，接着指出其报道与著名漫画家比尔·莫尔丁的作品异曲同工（paralleled）；本句由此总结“两人（Both men）都 [17] 战争的肮脏与疲惫”。emphasized 意为“强调；着重表现”，准确呼应上文对真实战场艰辛细节的着力刻画，故选[B]。
［错项排除］[A] neglected（忽视）和 [C] avoided（回避）均与上文派尔专注描写 dirt-snow-and-mud soldiers 的核心特点完全相反，故排除；[D] admired（钦佩；赞赏）作及物动词接“肮脏与疲惫（dirt and exhaustion）”，在语义情感上荒谬不通，作品刻画的是战争残酷而非赞美肮脏疲惫，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [18] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内语义与同位语列举概括。
［精准定位］...the [18] of civilization that the soldiers shared with each other and the civilians: coffee, tobacco, whiskey, shelter, sleep.
［解题思路］空格前出现并列宾语“战争的肮脏与疲惫”，后接冒号同位语列举“咖啡、烟草、威士忌、容身之所、片刻睡眠”。在残酷动荡的战火废墟中，这些零星微薄的日常物事正是文明生活遗落下来的吉光片羽与零碎点滴。fragments（碎片；零星片段）既概括了五类具体列举的共性，又以“文明残片”强化战时生活的匮乏与艰辛，故选[C]。
［错项排除］[A] stages（时期；阶段）无法概括咖啡、住所与睡眠等具体物质/状态例举，故排除；[B] illusions（幻想；错觉）与后文列举的真实可感物品（咖啡、烟草、威士忌、住所、睡眠）性质矛盾，故排除；[D] advances（进步；进展）多指文明或科技的新近突破发展，无法概括“睡眠、遮蔽所”这类基本生存需求且偏离战时艰苦语境，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [19] in the passage:
questions.explanation:
［考点提炼］句内逻辑与介词辨析。
［精准定位］[19] Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries, G.I. Joe was any American soldier, [20] the most important person in their lives.
［解题思路］句中代词 their 回指 Egypt, France, and a dozen more countries（的民众），指出大兵乔在战时是“他们生命中最重要的人”。这里需要一个介词引出持有某种观点、态度或情感归属的主体。To sb/some country 意为“对……而言；在……看来/心目中”，用于引出感受与评价主体，完美契合语境，故选[B]。
［错项排除］[A] With 表态度时多接承受态度的对象（如 happy with sth），而不能直接置于句首引出持有看法的国家民众主体，故排除；[C] Among 意为“在……之中”，引出观点群体时常与 common、popular 等形容词连用，本句并无此类对应词且易产生歧义，故排除；[D] Beyond 意为“超出（范围）；除……之外”，不能引出感知“最重要之人”的情感主体，故排除。

questions.stem: Choose the best option for blank [20] in the passage:
questions.explanation: 【命题解密】上下文语义与介词短语。空格修饰表语“the most important person in their lives”。at that point指代“在那个历史关头/在二战爆发的生死存亡时刻”，对于被纳粹铁蹄践踏而获得解放的各国民众而言，冲锋陷阵的美国大兵正是彼时他们生命中最重要的人，呼应开篇“that is not how it used to be”，故选[D]。[A] on the contrary（恰恰相反）逻辑转折不当；[B] by this means（以此方式）表手段；[C] from the outset（从一开始）超出二战特定时间范围。

questions.stem: It is implied in Paragraph 1 that nowadays homework

options.text: is no longer an educational ritual
options.content: is no longer an educational ritual

options.text: is not required for advanced courses
options.content: is not required for advanced courses

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】推理判断题。定位至第一段①句“Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned”。句中“has been particularly scorned（近年来尤其受到唾弃/受到指责）”与选项[A]“is receiving more criticism（正在受到更多批评）”构成同义替换，故选[A]。[B]项忽略否定词never，将文意彻底反向曲解；[C]项曲解②句“revising their thinking on this educational ritual”，学区只是在重新思考这一惯例，并未取消；[D]项与③句“with the exception of some advanced courses（高级课程除外）”完全相悖。

questions.stem: L.A. Unified has made the rule about homework mainly because poor students

options.text: tend to have moderate expectations for their education
options.content: tend to have moderate expectations for their education

options.text: have asked for a different educational standard
options.content: have asked for a different educational standard

options.text: may have problems finishing their homework
options.content: may have problems finishing their homework

options.text: have voiced their complaints about homework
options.content: have voiced their complaints about homework

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】事实细节题。定位至第二段①句“This rule is meant to address the difficulty that students from impoverished or chaotic homes might have in completing their homework”。句中“the difficulty... in completing their homework（来自贫困或混乱家庭的学生在完成作业方面可能遇到的困难）”与选项[C]“may have problems finishing their homework”完美同义对应，故选[C]。[A]项无中生有推断贫困生期望不高；[B]项将第四段作者指出的新规危险倾向“降低对贫困生的要求”颠倒为学生主动要求；[D]项并未提及贫困生大发抱怨。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 3, one problem with the policy is that it may

options.text: result in students’ indifference to their report cards
options.content: result in students’ indifference to their report cards

options.text: undermine the authority of state tests
options.content: undermine the authority of state tests

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】推理判断题。定位至第三段②句“But with homework counting for no more than 10% of their grades, students can easily skip half their homework and see very little difference on their report cards”。作者指出，由于家庭作业在总分中占比极低，学生即使少做一半作业在成绩单上也看不出任何区别，这必然会严重挫伤学生完成作业的积极性。选项[D]“discourage students from doing homework（打击学生做作业的积极性）”是对此处文意的准确归纳，故选[D]。[A]项混淆very little difference与indifference（漠不关心）；[B]项无端引申州考权威性受损；[C]项将未能授权教师夸大为限制权力。

questions.stem: As mentioned in Paragraph 4, a key question unanswered about homework is whether ______.

options.text: it places extra burdens on teachers
options.content: it places extra burdens on teachers

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】推理判断题。定位至第四段①至③句“the policy addresses none of the truly thorny questions about homework. If the district finds homework to be unimportant... it should move to reduce or eliminate... Conversely, if homework matters, it should account for a significant portion...”。作者借Conversely构成对称假设，批评学区新政既未承认作业重要，也未表明作业不重要，因而回避了“家庭作业在学校教育中究竟是否举足轻重”这一根本问题。选项[B]“whether it counts much in schooling（在学校教育中是否起重要作用）”精准概括了核心争论，故选[B]。[A]项仅是作业不重要假设下的举措；[C]项曲解了末句教师批改负担；[D]项将对学业成就的影响偷换为对成绩单本身。

questions.stem: A suitable title for this text could be ______.

options.text: A Welcomed Policy for Poor Students
options.content: A Welcomed Policy for Poor Students

options.text: Wrong Interpretations of an Educational Policy
options.content: Wrong Interpretations of an Educational Policy

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】主旨大意题。全文首段引出洛杉矶联合学区针对家庭作业所推行的死板硬性政策（an inflexible policy）；第二至四段逐层剖析该政策的致命缺陷：以保护贫困生为名行降低标准之实、一刀切的限比打消学生积极性、回避了家庭作业是否重要的核心实质；尾段得出明确结论：新规应当叫停搁置。全文始终聚焦于批评学区处理作业的错误方式，选项[A]“A Faulty Approach to Homework（处理家庭作业的一个错误方法）”完美契合主旨并鲜明呈现作者的批判态度，故选[A]。[B]项与作者抨击新规伤害贫困生相悖；[C]项偏离了对学区政策的批判重心；[D]项将对政策本身的批判篡改为外界对政策的误解。

questions.stem: By saying "it is...the rainbow" (Line 3, Para. 1), the author means pink ______.

options.text: cannot explain girls' lack of imagination
options.content: cannot explain girls' lack of imagination

options.text: should not be associated with girls' innocence
options.content: should not be associated with girls' innocence

options.text: should not be the sole representation of girlhood
options.content: should not be the sole representation of girlhood

options.text: cannot influence girls' lives and interests
options.content: cannot influence girls' lives and interests

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】词句推断题。
【精准定位】定位至首段②句“It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls' identity to appearance”。
作者以“七色彩虹中极小的一抹色彩”比喻粉色只是缤纷色彩中的一种，年轻女孩的生活与童年本应丰富多彩，不应让粉色成为女孩身份的唯一代表。[C]项“should not be the sole representation of girlhood（粉色不应成为少女时代的唯一代表）”准确传达了作者意图，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A]项“不能解释女孩想象力的匮乏”对应末句人们对女孩生活与兴趣缺乏想象力，偏离彩虹比喻本体；[B]项针对③句粉色被视为纯真证明，非“彩虹一小片”的喻义；[D]项“不能影响女孩的生活和兴趣”与首句“粉色充斥着年轻女孩的生活”相悖。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, which of the following is true of colours?

options.text: Colours are encoded in girls' DNA.
options.content: Colours are encoded in girls' DNA.

options.text: Blue used to be regarded as the colour for girls.
options.content: Blue used to be regarded as the colour for girls.

options.text: Pink used to be a neutral colour in symbolising genders.
options.content: Pink used to be a neutral colour in symbolising genders.

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】事实细节题。
【精准定位】定位至第二段④⑤句“When nursery colours were introduced, pink was actually considered the more masculine colour... Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised femininity”。
文中明确指出，当婴儿房颜色刚引入时，粉色其实被视为更具男子气概的颜色，而蓝色象征女性气质，即过去蓝色曾被视作女孩的颜色。[B]项“Blue used to be regarded as the colour for girls”与原文完全契合，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A]项与首句明确否定的“encoded in their DNA, it is not”直接相悖；[C]项曲解②句，婴儿穿白色是因为水煮漂洗的实际需要，而非婴儿偏爱；[D]项错把dress（gender-neutral dresses）张冠李戴给pink，文中明确说明pink曾被视为更偏男性的颜色（masculine colour），而非中性色。

questions.stem: The author suggests that our perception of children's psychological development was much influenced by ______.

options.text: the marketing of products for children
options.content: the marketing of products for children

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】事实细节题。
【精准定位】定位至第三段①至③句“I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns out, according to Daniel Cook, a historian of childhood consumerism, it was popularised as a marketing trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s”。
作者直白指出，商业营销趋势深刻支配了我们对儿童天性及心理发展的核心认知，甚至连“学步期（toddler）”也是1930年代服装制造商为促销发明的营销手段。[B]项“the marketing of products for children（针对儿童产品的市场营销）”精准对应，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A]项“对儿童天性的观察”只是受营销趋势支配的认知对象（what is natural to kids），并非原因；[C]项“对儿童行为的研究”在②句被作者以“wrong”明确否定；[D]项“儿童消费研究”偷换了童年消费主义历史学家Daniel Cook的身份背景。

questions.stem: We may learn from Paragraph 4 that department stores were advised to ______.

options.text: attach equal importance to different genders
options.content: attach equal importance to different genders

options.text: focus on infant wear and older kids' clothes
options.content: focus on infant wear and older kids' clothes

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】推理判断题。
【精准定位】定位至第四段①至③句“Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should create a 'third stepping stone' between infant wear and older kids' clothes... Splitting kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits”。
行业刊物建议百货商店在婴儿服与大童装之间增设“学步童装”这一中间层级，并将儿童乃至成人不断切分为更细小的类别来刺激利润。[A]项“classify consumers into smaller groups（将消费者划分为更小的群体）”精准概括了这一细分市场策略，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B]项与末句“放大甚至凭空捏造性别差异（magnify gender differences）”相悖；[C]项仅截取比较参照物infant wear和older kids' clothes，建议实质是在二者之间开辟新分类；[D]项将结果当建议，common shoppers' term是推行分类后的附带结果。

questions.stem: It can be concluded that girls' attraction to pink seems to be ______.

options.text: clearly explained by their inborn tendency
options.content: clearly explained by their inborn tendency

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】推理概括题。
【精准定位】综合全篇主旨，作者在第二段推翻了“粉色吸引力刻在女孩DNA里”的成见，并在第二至四段指出直到20世纪80年代中期商家将放大年龄与性别差异作为主导营销策略后，粉色才被塑造成定义女孩的特质；服装商为了利润甚至创造出“toddler”等细分类别。
由此可知，女孩对粉色的迷恋主要由追逐利润的商人通过营销手段强加塑造而来，故选[C] mainly imposed by profit-driven businessmen。
【错项排除】[A]项曲解了服装商的作用，商家利用营销技巧制造消费需求而非学术理解女孩天性；[B]项“由先天倾向清楚解释”与第二段“it is not（encoded in their DNA）”直接相悖；[D]项“得到心理学家很好阐释”与第三段明确否定的“experts developed after years of research: wrong”相反。

questions.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that the biotech companies would like ______.

options.text: the BIO to issue a warning
options.content: the BIO to issue a warning

options.text: judges to rule out gene patenting
options.content: judges to rule out gene patenting

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】推理引申题。
【精准定位】定位至首段②至⑤句“Companies had won patents for isolated DNA for decades... But in March 2010 a judge ruled that genes were unpatentable. Executives were violently agitated. The Biotechnology Industry Organisation (BIO), a trade group, assured members that this was just a 'preliminary step' in a longer battle”。
几十年来生物技术公司一直拥有分离DNA的专利权；2010年3月法官裁定基因不可申请专利后，高管们反应剧烈、极其愤怒，行业协会BIO也向成员保证这只是漫长抗争的“第一步”。由此反推，生物技术公司迫切希望基因能够申请专利。[A]项“genes to be patentable”准确概括其利益诉求，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B]项曲解了BIO的表态，BIO是向成员保证并安抚信心而非发出警告；[C]项将Executives were violently agitated（极其焦虑愤怒）曲解为希望高管活跃起来；[D]项与生物技术公司的诉求完全相反。

questions.stem: Those who are against gene patents believe that ______.

options.text: patents on genes depend much on innovation
options.content: patents on genes depend much on innovation

options.text: courts should restrict access to genetic tests
options.content: courts should restrict access to genetic tests

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】人物观点题。
【精准定位】定位至第三段③句“Critics make three main arguments against gene patents: a gene is a product of nature, so it may not be patented; gene patents suppress innovation rather than reward it; and patents' monopolies restrict access to genetic tests such as Myriad's”。
反对者提出的三点理由之一是“基因是自然产物，因此不可申请专利”，亦即只有人工造物才具备专利资格。[B]项“only man-made products are patentable”正是这一观点的反向同义改写，故选[B]。
【错项排除】[A]项文中并未质疑基因检测的可靠性；[C]项与反对者第二条理由“基因专利抑制（suppress）而非奖励创新”逻辑倒置；[D]项将反对者批评专利垄断限制（restrict access）基因检测使用，歪曲为法院应当限制。

questions.stem: According to Hans Sauer, companies are eager to win patents for ______.
questions.explanation:
【命题解密】人物观点题。
【精准定位】定位至第五段③④句“Firms are now studying how genes interact, looking for correlations that might be used to determine the causes of disease or predict a drug's efficacy. Companies are eager to win patents for 'connecting the dots,' explains Hans Sauer, a lawyer for the BIO”。
Hans Sauer所说的“connecting the dots（连点成线）”紧承上一句，其中dots指单个基因，即企业急于为发现基因间如何相互作用（how genes interact）从而建立关联申请专利。[A]项“discovering gene interactions”准确揭示了这一比喻，故选[A]。
【错项排除】[B]项“establishing disease correlations”杂糅了disease与correlations，原文looking for correlations指向基因间关联，用于确定疾病成因而非疾病本身间的关联；[C]项“绘制基因图”对connecting the dots望文生义；[D]项“识别人类DNA”属于旧式分子专利，第②句明确指出公司已不太可能继续大量申请人类DNA分子专利。

questions.stem: By saying "Each meeting was packed" (Line 4, Para. 6), the author means that ______.

options.text: the BIO was a powerful organisation
options.content: the BIO was a powerful organisation

options.text: gene patenting was a great concern
options.content: gene patenting was a great concern

options.text: lawyers were keen to attend conventions
options.content: lawyers were keen to attend conventions

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】句意推断题。
【精准定位】定位至第六段②③句“The BIO recently held a convention which included sessions to coach lawyers on the shifting landscape for patents. Each meeting was packed”。
BIO举办大会并专门开设分场培训律师应对不断变化的专利形势，结果每场会议都座无虚席（Each meeting was packed）。结合前文最高法院将听审Mayo案及基因专利战旷日持久的语境，可见“每场座无虚席”旨在说明整个行业与法律界对基因专利归属问题的高度关注。[C]项“gene patenting was a great concern”揭示了深层含义，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A]项“最高法院极具权威”虽相关但并非培训会爆满的原因；[B]项“BIO组织强大”脱离文章基因专利战主旨；[D]项仅停留在律师热衷参会的表面现象。

questions.stem: Generally speaking, the author's attitude toward gene patenting is ______.
questions.explanation:
【命题解密】观点态度题。
【精准定位】纵观全文，作者首先陈述2010年法官裁定基因不可获专利引发业内震动，随后第二段客观报道上诉法院推翻前判及Myriad公司称其为公司与患者的福音，第三至四段如实列出反对者的三大理由、司法部意见以及尚存争议，第五至六段进一步说明行业转向“连点”专利及最高法院即将审理的新讼案。
全文既不偏袒生物技术公司，也不盲从反对者，而是平实严谨地报道双方交锋与案件走向，态度完全客观中立，故选[D] objective。
【错项排除】[A] critical（批判的）与[C] scornful（鄙夷的）均带负面偏见，原文未流露否定；[B] supportive（支持的）忽略了作者大篇幅呈递反对声音及司法不确定性。

questions.stem: By saying "to find silver linings" (Line 1, Para. 2) the author suggests that the jobless try to ______.

options.text: make profits from the troubled economy
options.content: make profits from the troubled economy

options.text: look on the bright side of the recession
options.content: look on the bright side of the recession

questions.explanation: 【命题解密】词句推断题。定位至第二段①②句“No one tries harder than the jobless to find silver linings in this national economic disaster. Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways; they had become less materialistic...”。英语成语every cloud has a silver lining意为“黑暗中总有一丝光明”。后文具体解释失业者虽然痛苦，但也在努力寻找积极意义（如变得节俭、关爱家人）。选项[D]“look on the bright side of the recession（看到经济萧条中积极光明的一面）”与find silver linings语义完全一致，故选[D]。[A]寻求补贴、[B]牟取暴利、[C]探究失业原因均与语境无关。

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 2, the recession has made people ______.
questions.explanation:
【命题解密】事实细节题。
【精准定位】定位至第二段②至④句“Many said that unemployment, while extremely painful, had improved them in some ways: they had become less materialistic and more financially prudent; they were more aware of the struggles of others... At the very least, it has awoken us from our national fever dream of easy riches and bigger houses, and put a necessary end to an era of reckless personal spending”。
失业者变得不那么贪图物质、理财更为审慎，且大衰退把人们从轻轻松松发财买大房的狂热美梦中惊醒，结束了盲目挥霍的时代。可见大衰退促使人们反思并重新审视自己的生活方式与消费观，故选[D] reconsider their lifestyle。
【错项排除】[A]项曲解more aware of the struggles of others（更加体谅他人的艰辛），并非彼此斗争；[B]项将awoken us from our national fever dream（从狂热美梦中醒来）反向曲解为实现梦想；[C]项将more financially prudent（在财务上更加审慎）歪曲为质疑自己的审慎。

questions.stem: Benjamin Friedman believes that economic recessions may ______.

options.text: impose a heavier burden on immigrants
options.content: impose a heavier burden on immigrants

options.text: bring out more evils of human nature
options.content: bring out more evils of human nature

options.text: promote the advance of rights and freedoms
options.content: promote the advance of rights and freedoms

options.text: ease conflicts between races and classes
options.content: ease conflicts between races and classes

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】事实细节题。
【精准定位】定位至第三段②③句“Benjamin Friedman argues that both inside and outside the U.S., lengthy periods of economic stagnation or decline have almost always left society more mean-spirited and less inclusive, and have usually stopped or reversed the advance of rights and freedoms. Anti-immigrant sentiment typically increases, as does conflict between races and classes”。
弗里德曼指出，长期的经济停滞或衰退几乎总是令社会变得更狭隘刻薄（mean-spirited）、包容性更差，权利与自由受阻甚至倒退，排外与种族阶级冲突加剧。这些均体现经济衰退会激发和暴露出人性中更多丑恶的一面，故选[B] bring out more evils of human nature。
【错项排除】[A]项将排外情绪升高（Anti-immigrant sentiment increases）偷换为对移民施加更大负担；[C]项与原文stopped or reversed（受阻或倒退）彻底相反；[D]项与conflict... typically increases（冲突加剧）完全相悖。

questions.stem: The research of Till Von Wachter suggests that in the recession graduates from elite universities tend to ______.

options.text: lag behind the others due to decreased opportunities
options.content: lag behind the others due to decreased opportunities

options.text: catch up quickly with experienced employees
options.content: catch up quickly with experienced employees

options.text: see their life chances as dimmed as the others'
options.content: see their life chances as dimmed as the others'

options.text: recover more quickly than the others
options.content: recover more quickly than the others

questions.explanation:
【命题解密】事实细节题。
【精准定位】定位至第四段③句“The research of Till Von Wachter... suggests that not all people graduating into a recession see their life chances dimmed: those with degrees from elite universities catch up fairly quickly to where they otherwise would have been if they had graduated in better times; it is the masses beneath them that are left behind”。
研究证实名校毕业生能够相当迅速地追回在经济繁荣时期毕业本应达到的职业水平，而落后的是其下的普通大众。即名校毕业生比其他人恢复得更快，故选[D] recover more quickly than the others。
【错项排除】[A]项把are left behind的主语由普通大众（the masses）张冠李戴为名校毕业生；[B]项把catch up to的对象由“繁荣期毕业本应达到的水平”篡改为“有经验的老员工”；[C]项忽略句首否定not all people，颠倒了名校生与其他人的差异。

questions.stem: The author thinks that the influence of hard times on society is ______.
questions.explanation:
【命题解密】观点态度题。
【精准定位】定位至第五段④⑤句“We will have to wait and see exactly how these hard times will reshape our social fabric. But they certainly will reshape it, and all the more so the longer they extend”。
作者指出，艰难时期究竟会如何重塑社会结构尚需观望，但可以确定的是，它一定会重塑社会结构，而且持续时间越长影响越深。因此作者认为艰难时期对社会的影响是确定无疑的（certain），故选[C]。
【错项排除】[A]项trivial（微不足道的）与首段及末段强调深刻重塑社会相悖；[B]项positive（积极的）和[D]项destructive（毁灭性的）均以偏概全，文章第二段提到有限的积极面，三、四段分析负面效应，但末段明确表示具体形态尚未可知、唯独重塑本身确定无疑。

In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue, mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders”。马基雅维利在《君主论》中主张狡诈、无情与果决，而不是仁慈、正义或道德美德，颠覆了传统的英雄传记传统。选项[F]“dismissed virtue as unnecessary for successful leaders（认为美德对成功的领导者是不必要的）”是对championed... rather than virtue的精准概括，故选[F]。

【精准定位】定位至第五段（即原文倒数第三段）“This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte. These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals”。
维多利亚时期思想家托马斯·卡莱尔认为斯迈尔斯的实用主义传记过于中产阶级化，他将笔墨专门聚焦于马丁·路德、奥利弗·克伦威尔和拿破仑等真正的英雄人物，认为这些划时代伟人的人生是难以效仿的。选项[C]“focused on epochal figures whose lives were hard to imitate”直接对应原文These epochal figures represented lives hard to imitate，故选[C]。
【错项排除】[D]项“opened up new realms of understanding...”出自末段，那是批判卡莱尔英雄史观、转向“自下而上的民众史观”的当代英国史学家（替代卡莱尔者）所开启的新领域，且原文指理解历史的新领域而非伟人。

【精准定位】定位至第六段“Not everyone was convinced by such bombast. 'The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles,' wrote Marx and Engels in The Communist Manifesto... And history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle”。
针对卡莱尔夸大伟人权威的言论，马克思和恩格斯在《共产党宣言》中明确提出历史是阶级斗争的历史，创造财富和进行斗争的是现实的、活生生的人，因此历史应当是人民大众及其斗争记录的故事。选项[E]“held that history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle”在文中原句复现，故选[E]。
